### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **53** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (44 routes)`, `recordId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `037de658c136ba076825e4eb83c5b5baa715645d` — the merge of head `e6dc0654ef767c6a3efe5c0bdd3ef94a8aa73b32` into base `e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 037de658c136ba076825e4eb83c5b5baa715645d && git checkout 037de658c136ba076825e4eb83c5b5baa715645d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a e6dc0654ef767c6a3efe5c0bdd3ef94a8aa73b32 && git checkout -B drift-repro e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a && git merge --no-ff e6dc0654ef767c6a3efe5c0bdd3ef94a8aa73b32

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e627eaa171f17d7b439cc385fe5c14ace5a85f7a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1683e99c150e74361147a3559136c5347c22c766`
Local-runs: none
Scope: content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, content/docs/ui/actions.mdx, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/api-backend.json, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/tool-confirmation-prescription-tense.pin.test.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (the published `run_action` input schema and the bridge's one first-party caller), packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (declared `params[]`), packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts (`AIActionConfirmation`), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (`standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus`), packages/spec/src/kernel/address-grammar.ts (`readNamespacePositionSegment`), packages/types/src/actions-door-answer.ts (`actionsDoorAnswerOf`), packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts (`resolveActionHandlerKeys`), packages/runtime/src/object-value-shape.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, and `origin/main`'s packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts and action-execution.ts as the base of the move. The changeset is the prose face: read for ②, not reviewed.

Inputs read: card #31923 body and all 7 comments (ruling 6741181718 included), PR #32032 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...1683e99c` (17 files), the check-runs on the head. Check-runs at review time: 25 success, 12 skipped, 1 cancelled (a superseded `PR-body guards` run; its sibling is success), 31 in progress, 0 failed. `Check Changeset` (both), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are success. Build, lint, type-check and every Test Core shard had not concluded, so no gate family they carry is asserted here.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Public surface, widened: `dispatchAction` plus the types `ActionDispatchRequest`, `ActionDispatchAnswer`, `ActionDispatchPosture` leave the package root (`src/index.ts`); `package.json` `exports` is untouched. Right, and it is the names ruling 6741181718 Q2 fixed. One member is beyond that ruling's list: `namespace` (see ③). One more public entry is not named anywhere: `HttpDispatcher.dispatchHostAction` is a public method on an exported class (nit, ④ F4).
2. REST `/actions` accept set and answers: unchanged. Right. Read gate by gate against `origin/main`'s `handleActionsRequest` and `dispatchAdmittedRestAction`: floor, 405, path parse, activation write door, disabled-object check before resolution, then 409 candidates, 503 degraded, 404 undeclared, D4 403, activation 409, owner gate, type 400, flow 503, body / `params` / `recordId` 400, ADR-0104 400, subject load, and the four arms with the same envelopes and the same invocation row (`surface: 'rest'`). Two differences, neither on the wire: the actor display-name lookup now runs after the declarative and api arms and inside the arm's `try`; the script arm re-checks the engine, which the door already refused `503` for.
3. MCP `run_action` accept set: narrowed by exactly one value, an array `params`. Right, and complete as far as the tree shows. Checked for a second narrowing and found none: the prelude still reads a string `params` as empty and a non-string `recordId` as absent before the shared shape checks see them; `headlessActionTypeError` + the flow 503 + `isHeadlessInvokableAction(…, true)` admit the same set the old single invokability check admitted; `resolveActionHandlerKeys(action, name)` adds no key, because the by-name resolution guarantees `action.name === name` and the fallback is deduped; the new pre-resolution disabled-object check swallows every error but `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`; `null` params never reaches the shape check at MCP.
4. MCP refusals that move (C3, C4, C5 and its disabled sibling, C6 and its unexposed sibling, C7, R1): each was refused on base and is refused on head; only status, code, sentence or `details` moved to the REST door's. Right, and not a narrowing, as ruling 6741181718 Q1 holds. C6 and C7 are beyond the four rows that ruling names; both are listed, pinned and of the same kind. Not listed, same kind: the `sys_*` exposure, `ai.exposed` and unbound-script refusals are now thrown with `code` + `status` where base threw a bare `Error`. The tool's answer is the same `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (the reader's terminal arm answered that for an uncoded `Error`); only an embedder reading the thrown value sees the new members.
5. Invocation rows: a host call writes one row with no `surface`; REST still writes `rest`, MCP `mcp`. Right against ruling Q3 and the optional `ExecutionContext.surface`.
6. Gate ledgers: `check-route-envelope` lowers `actions.ts` 3 to 1 and counts the two moved relays in `action-dispatch.ts` through `DISPATCHER_SHARED_FILES` (total conserved, the file is scanned, a missing path is an error). Right, and the better answer to round 1's open question. `system-context.mdx` row 52 gains `dispatchActionRequest`, whose first statement is the anonymous floor. Right.
7. The spec pin test re-point reads the gate where it now lives: the door enters as `ai`, the gate sits under `posture === 'ai'` in the admission half, the refusal returns before dispatch, REST enters as `rest`. At least as strong as before. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch`. Right: `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (nothing a metadata author can write changes), and AGENTS.md ships a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, as `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` stands line-initial on both the PR body and the changeset, and matches the diff: one export widened, one accept set narrowed. The ADR-0087 marker is present (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) and its reason is true: no stored shape changes. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — matches what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round 1 `open_questions` (route-envelope census, A keep vs B add the file): answered B in the tree. Agreed, see ① 6. Round 2 carries none.
- `security_findings: "withheld"` in both dev reports: not in this review's inputs and not covered by this record. Escalated to the seat, which reads them by its own channel before it adopts.
- Rulings cited by the PR body that are not on the card thread: seat 1's Q6 / Q7 answers (Q6 adds the public member `namespace`), the seat review S1 (the Clause-② arm moved from the ruled `yes (widening)` to `yes (narrowing)`) and S2 (the gate edit). The claim on the card still reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `No packages/spec/**`, while the diff edits a spec test file, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`, the engine-double ledger and a checklist anchor. Each change is sound on its merits (the narrowing arm is the true one; `namespace` is needed for the addressed REST path to have an equal). Escalated: the seat posts one claim amendment on the card that records Q6, the arm change and the widened file surface, so the card is the record.
- `dogfood_battery: n/a` on a head that now declares a `(narrowing)` arm, with the dogfood closure run on the round-1 head only. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is success on this head. Whether the battery is owed for an arm with a first-party count of 0 is the seat's call.
- Dev deviations (attribution block before `Fixes`, the two `import '@objectstack/metadata'` lines, the engine-double pin): accepted, gate-driven.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no relay note owed. The PR is a draft; 31 check-runs were still running, so the all-green landing check remains the seat's.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, against the published spec on `main`: it makes the spec's own refusal real, and takes no declared capability away. An action's params are declared by name (`ActionSchema.params[]`), and ADR-0104 closes the bag against those names; an array bag has no declared meaning. The published `run_action` input schema on `main` is `params: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (`mcp-http-tools.ts`), and the REST door on `main` already refuses a non-object bag (`#25976`). Base spread an array into the keys `"0"`, `"1"`, which the strict contract refused on every action that declares params, so the only calls that ran were on handler actions with none, which received junk keys. Tried to break it: the realistic loser is an embedder that sends `params: []` to mean "none"; it now gets a located `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` and the fix is `{}` or omitting the key. No first-party caller can reach the bridge with an array. Holds.

The shared sequence against the code it replaces: holds (① 2 to 4). The card's "Done when" is met in the tree: the export leaves the root, `action-dispatch.test.ts` proves equality with the REST door for a gated action and an elevated flow with equal ran-counts, and `actions.mdx` names it.

Findings:

- **F1, should-fix.** `dispatchActionRequest` reads the posture as `request.posture === 'ai' ? 'ai' : 'rest'`. Any other value, such as `'AI'`, `'mcp'` or a mis-wired config string, silently selects the weaker rule set: no `sys_*` exposure, no `ai.exposed`, no confirmation gate. The type closes this for a typed caller only, and the same function already defends `actionName` and `credentialHeaders` at run time. The posture selects security gates for the named consumer, an AI tool, so an unknown value should be refused `400` before anything resolves, with one pin. It is not a must-fix: the declared contract (`'rest' | 'ai'`, default `'rest'`) is implemented as written.
- **F2, nit.** `dispatchAction` builds its own `HttpDispatcher(kernel)` and a context with no `kernel` and no `dataDriver`, and never runs `resolveRequestScope`. On a single-kernel host this is the REST door's context exactly, which is what the tests prove. On a multi-kernel host the "byte for byte" claim rests on the resolver being registered as the `kernel-resolver` service and honouring a context that carries only `environmentId`; if it yields nothing, the call falls back to the kernel passed in, where REST would have been placed by the resolver first. Nothing in the tree is wrong; the doc does not say which kernel to pass, and no pin covers a resolver. A follow-up card, to settle in cloud's pin round before the mirror is deleted.
- **F3, nit.** Under `ai`, an entitled agent now receives the REST door's type prescription: for an off-origin `api` action "Call `TARGET` directly (METHOD)", for a client-side action its `target`. Base answered an agent "cannot be invoked via MCP" and named neither. And a never-exposed client-side action is now told to add `ai.exposed`, which could not make it runnable. Still refused, same status. A follow-up card for an `ai`-posture sentence.
- **F4, nit, prose faces.** The changeset states the narrowing without the `**BREAKING**` banner the PR body carries, and does not name `HttpDispatcher.dispatchHostAction`. `actions.mdx` does not mention `credentialHeaders` or `environmentId`, the first of which the card's Ask 1 names. The PR body's table lists C2 and C10 as unchanged without saying the thrown value gained `code` + `status`.

No must-fix. F1 earns a delta review of its fix; F2 to F4 are accepted deviations, follow-up cards or prose-face edits.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e6dc0654ef767c6a3efe5c0bdd3ef94a8aa73b32`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.test.ts, .changeset/31923-headless-action-dispatch.md, content/docs/ui/actions.mdx; every other path is unchanged since 1683e99c

Delta review of record 6757903087 (head 1683e99c: PASS, with one should-fix and three nits). This head adds two commits, acc37ce2 and e6dc0654, with no merge and no rebase. The PR body is patched (the thread's issue_patch, read back byte for byte).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **F1 is closed.** `dispatchActionRequest` now accepts only `posture` undefined, `'rest'` or `'ai'`. Any other value is answered `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `details` on field `posture` (`invalid_option`). That happens after the `actionName` check and before any header copy, resolution or arm, so nothing runs and no row is written. The arm reads the checked value. Pinned for `'AI'`, `'mcp'`, `''` and `1`, with `rest`, `ai` and absent as 200 controls. The thread's ablation A15 (check removed) turned the pin red, and the change was restored.
2. **The host export's accept set narrows by those off-type values.** It is new in this PR, so no released caller moves. Right, and it is what F1 asked for.
3. **F4 is closed on the prose faces.**
   - The changeset carries the **BREAKING (narrowing)** banner for the array `params` at the MCP bridge. It also names `HttpDispatcher.dispatchHostAction` and the posture refusal.
   - `actions.mdx` names `environmentId`, `credentialHeaders` and the posture refusal.
   - The PR table notes that C2 and C10 now throw with `code` `VALIDATION_ERROR` (from `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(400)`) and `status` 400.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `patch` on `@objectstack/runtime`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on both carriers, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the ADR-0087 marker.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The claim amendment is on the card.** It records Q6, Q7, S1 and S2 and the surface past the claim.
- **Dogfood:** not rerun, by seat ruling. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run on 1683e99c was success, and this head's run decides.
- **`security_findings`:** the thread confirms there are none.
- **F2 and F3** go to a follow-up card the seat files after landing.
- **Gates rerun on this head (thread report), all exit 0:**
  - 3 test files, 362 tests, plus the spec confirmation pin;
  - tsc and eslint;
  - the changeset family;
  - the docs family;
  - route-envelope.

### ④ Design judgment

No new finding. The posture check fails closed: an unrecognised value no longer picks the weaker rules.

Check-runs on this head were still running when this record was written. Landing waits for them to finish all green.
